framework: China - Measures for Labeling AI-Generated Synthetic Content (Doc. No. Guoxinban Tongzi [2025] No. 2; in force 1 Sep 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: On user request, providers may supply generated content without explicit labels after the user agreement sets out the user's labelling obligations and responsibility for use, and must keep related logs, including recipient information, for at least six months.
what_is_tested: Log retention

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: A provider that concludes an Annex III system is not high-risk (e.g. narrow procedural task) must document that assessment before placing it on the market, register it under Art. 49(2) and give it to authorities on request; profiling systems always stay high-risk.
what_is_tested: The provider's own classification assessment (documented self-assessment)
who_tests: Provider (self-assessment); national competent authorities may request

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Commission must issue standardisation requests covering all Section 2 requirements and request deliverables facilitating joint compliance with Chapter III Sections 2-3 and Annex I product legislation.
what_is_tested: Standardisation request (a duty on the Commission)
who_tests: European Commission (requesting); European standardisation organisations (CEN, CENELEC, ETSI)

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Member States may allow real-world testing outside sandboxes of AI-enabled products under Annex I Section B legislation, through national frameworks that require a mandatory testing plan agreed with the authority and apply most Art. 60 safeguards.
what_is_tested: Real-world testing of Section B products

framework: EU AI Act - Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content (Section 1, providers)
requirement_paraphrase: Signatories measure detection accuracy (e.g. error rates) on varied samples, including other systems' content and data not used in training, across content length, size, diversity and semantics; they also test robustness to common processing operations (compression, cropping, paraphrasing, translation, print-and-scan) and to adversarial attacks (copying, removal, regeneration, modification of marks) using the same metrics; compliance is demonstrated before market placement and over the lifecycle.
what_is_tested: Reliability and robustness metrics for watermark/marking detection

framework: EU harmonised standards work (CEN-CENELEC JTC 21)
requirement_paraphrase: The AI trustworthiness framework series is at mixed stages: Part 1 logging at stage 50, Part 3 human oversight at stage 40, Parts 2 (transparency), 4 (accuracy) and 5 (robustness) at stage 20; all flagged harmonised, none OJEU-referenced.
what_is_tested: Logging, transparency, oversight, accuracy, robustness

framework: Japan - AI Promotion Act (Act No. 53 of 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Government is to collect information on AI trends, analyse cases where AI misuse infringed rights, and give guidance, advice and information to businesses and others based on findings.
what_is_tested: Post-incident analysis of rights infringement cases (not pre-deployment testing)

framework: South Korea - AI Framework Act (AI Basic Act)
requirement_paraphrase: Minister of Science and ICT may operate an AI Safety Institute covering risk analysis, evaluation criteria and methods, safety technology and standardisation, and support under Art. 32.
what_is_tested: AI safety risk analysis and evaluation methods

framework: SDAIA AI Ethics Principles (Version 1.0, September 2023, read on dgp.sdaia.gov.sa; the 2025 edition on sdaia.gov.sa was not readable)
clause_or_page: Annexure C (AI Ethics Checklist), approx. pp. 41-46; layout scrambled in extraction, low confidence
requirement_paraphrase: Provides a lifecycle checklist (Plan and Design, Prepare Input Data, Build and Validate, Deploy and Monitor) with a column marking whether each item is binding for third parties.
what_is_tested: Self-assessment questions on oversight, risk, testing, monitoring
who_tests: Adopting entity (self) and third parties for flagged items

framework: Singapore IMDA Starter Kit for Testing LLM-Based Applications for Safety and Reliability (v1.0, January 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Set pass thresholds before testing (to avoid moving goalposts) and refine them after testing only on evidence; thresholds are specific to each app and organisation.
what_is_tested: Acceptance threshold setting
who_tests: Developer / deployer (each organisation sets its own threshold)

framework: Singapore Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI (version read: v1.0, 22 Jan 2026; v1.5 not read)
requirement_paraphrase: Test in real or realistic environments that mirror production (balancing realism against risk of real-world side effects), test repeatedly across varied datasets to observe low-probability behaviours and stability, and evaluate results at scale using different methods per workflow part; the source describes current industry solutions as LLM or agent evaluators, or human evaluation (practice described, not a recommendation).
what_is_tested: Realistic-environment and stochastic testing

framework: DIFC Data Protection Regulations, Consolidated Version No. 2, Regulation 10 (autonomous and semi-autonomous systems)
requirement_paraphrase: Deployer/Operator must provide on request evidence of algorithms that make the System seek human intervention where processing may have an unfair or discriminatory impact, together with a risk and impact assessment of unjust bias or High Risk Processing arising from the System's inputs.
what_is_tested: Bias/unfair-impact risk and impact assessment; human-intervention triggers
who_tests: Deployer/Operator (self-assessment, available to affected party on request)

framework: Smart Dubai AI Ethics Principles & Guidelines (Guidelines changelog to v1.11; v1.6 is the Principles changelog)
requirement_paraphrase: AI developer and operator organisations should undertake reasonable data exploration and/or testing to identify prejudicial decision-making tendencies caused by bias in data.
what_is_tested: Bias in data and resulting decisions
who_tests: AI developer and AI operator organisations

framework: Dubai AI Ethics Toolkit self-assessment tool (Digital Dubai)
clause_or_page: Page section 'What is the self-assessment tool for?'
requirement_paraphrase: The page advises against implementing an AI system unless a certain level of ethics performance is reached; 'should' guidelines weigh more than 'should consider' guidelines in the score.
what_is_tested: Ethics performance score before implementation

framework: Dubai Department of Finance AI Policy (Arabic)
requirement_paraphrase: The Department commits to identify, assess and manage risks of its AI systems (technical, regulatory, ethical, bias, misuse) and to feed impact assessment results into risk management.
what_is_tested: Risks of the Department's AI systems

framework: UAE AI Ethics: Principles & Guidelines (Dec 2022)
clause_or_page: s3.8.2.2 body text, p.42 (heading concerns an oversight mechanism for data)
requirement_paraphrase: Privacy impact assessments should be conducted and also cover societal and ethical considerations.
what_is_tested: Privacy impact of AI system

framework: UK AI Playbook for the UK Government (GDS, published 2025-02-10)
requirement_paraphrase: Once released, keep ongoing performance monitoring with evidence that the system operates as expected; use managed release processes with the ability to withdraw and revert; monitor for model drift.
what_is_tested: Post-release performance monitoring and rollback

framework: Frontier AI Safety Commitments, AI Seoul Summit 2024 (company commitments published by UK DSIT on GOV.UK; page updated 7 February 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Set thresholds at which severe risks are intolerable, assess whether thresholds have been breached, articulate mitigations, and follow explicit processes if thresholds are met, in the extreme not developing or deploying a model if mitigations cannot keep risk below thresholds.
what_is_tested: Severe-risk threshold breach assessment

framework: US NIST AI 600-1 Generative AI Profile (July 2024)
requirement_paraphrase: Conduct AI red-teaming for privacy issues such as output of training data, model extraction, membership inference, revealing confidential or personal information, and tracking user location.
what_is_tested: Privacy leakage
who_tests: Red teams (with TEVV actors and domain experts)

framework: US OMB Memorandum M-25-21 (3 April 2025) - federal agency use of AI [added beyond assigned scope]
requirement_paraphrase: Complete a documented AI impact assessment before deploying a high-impact use case, covering purpose and benefits, data quality, impacts on privacy/civil rights, reassessment schedule, costs, results of an independent review by a reviewer within the agency not involved in development, and signed risk acceptance.
what_is_tested: Impact assessment with internal independent review
who_tests: Agency; independent reviewer inside the agency
